set.descent_text: The second pitch follows a crack and corner, then angles left to the ridge above a roomy ledge. From the ridge, scramble down to climber's left to get off.

review.notes: Route page states the finish at the ridge and the scramble down on climber's left.

set.descent_text: The third pitch works left through hand cracks to a pine, steps behind it and climbs ledges to meet the northeast ridge part way up its steep section. A shorter alternative traverses hard left across the face to the ridge. Either way, finish by scrambling off to climber's left.

review.notes: Route page gives both finishes and the scramble off to climber's left.

set.approach: From the Twin Lakes trailhead, follow the main trail past the turn-off for the Hulk to Blarney Lake, where the buttress can be picked out from the shore. Continue to Peeler Lake, staying right at the Crown Lake junction, then cut left and circle the lake's western shore. Pick a way across the talus to the slopes beneath the buttress; the loose footing calls for care.

review.notes: Area page and a second guide agree on the trail, Blarney Lake, Crown Lake junction and western shore. Distance and time left out (sources share wording). No page describes this line's own start or descent.

set.approach: From the Twin Lakes parking area, walk through the campground and take the Robinson Creek trail west until Little Slide Canyon opens up to your left. Leave the trail at a shady resting spot, head south through a meadow, cross the creek on a big log and climb the hillside into the canyon. A band of cliffs crosses the canyon; a third-class gully gets through it, or use the scree on either side if snow fills the gullies. Continue to the head of the canyon, where an easy talus scramble leads to the base of the Regge Pole.

review.notes: Canyon approach from the area page, confirmed by the AAJ note (head of Little Slide Canyon from Twin Lakes); talus scramble to the tower from the spire page. Which side the line starts on is not stated by a page I could open; no descent stated.

set.approach: The usual way in is from the east, starting at the Pine Creek Pass trailhead. Follow the trail past Upper Pine Lake, bend toward Honeymoon Lake and continue into Granite Park, then cross Granite Bear Pass near 12,400 feet. West of the pass, go between Big Bear Lake (to the north) and Little Bear Lake (to the south), trend southwest past a few tarns to Vee Lake, and follow the stream flowing out of it to the East Fork of Bear Creek. From there, climb cross-country up to the east side of the peak. Navigation off the trail needs care.

review.notes: Both pages give the same east-side approach; distance and gain left out (one wording). No page states where this line starts or how it descends.

set.approach: Reach Miter Basin over Cottonwood Pass, Old or New Army Pass, or Arc Pass; the Cottonwood way is the longer, gentler two-day option with a camp at Chicken Spring Lake, while crossing Old Army Pass from Horseshoe Meadows and dropping to Soldier Lake is the shorter, harder one. Camp anywhere in the basin. The Sky Blue Diamond stands directly south of Sky Blue Lake, the fourth formation counting from the south end of the group. Altared State starts to the right of the A-frame crack that splits the headwall. Scramble up from the base to a large ledge running across the right side of the formation, with one short fourth-class move, and start from there.
set.descent_text: Reverse the upper pitches to the descent ledge above the Diamond, using a series of downclimbs and a couple of rappels. Alternatively, from the big ledge reached after the fourth pitch, a non-technical walk-off leads north back toward the base; continuing to the summit means the technical way back to that ledge.

review.notes: Route page and the Stupa Troopers page agree on the descent ledge and the north walk-off. Rappel count left out (single source).

set.approach: From the May Lake trailhead, either make a rising traverse across from the lake or follow a faint, unmaintained trail to the foot of the cliffs and climb straight up. The buttress lies north-northeast of the lake and the orange rock is easy to spot. Clean Living starts at a vertical crack system about midway between Taphophobia and Fear of Flying.

review.notes: Area page for access, route page for the start. No descent stated.
